## Professional Summary

Vahid Faraji is a Senior Applied AI Specialist with 8 years in industry (2 in applied AI, 6 in data products and business analysis) plus 4 years in research. He bridges research and production, publishing peer-reviewed papers at ACM while deploying enterprise-scale multi-agent systems. His work focuses on context engineering, MCP-based agent architectures, and open-source AI tooling.

## Agent Engineering

- Agent harnesses built end to end: execution loops, tool interfaces and tool calling, context and memory, and agent skills
- Multi-step execution and multi-agent orchestration (planner, search, extraction and evaluation agents over MCP)
- Evals built from real tasks, with tracing and failure analysis used to decide what to change next
- Production ownership: reliability, latency and cost; resumable long-running tasks; tool-failure handling; user visibility and control over agent actions
- Experiments across models, prompting strategies, retrieval approaches and orchestration patterns, measured against outcomes
- Spec-driven design and implementation: writes the spec, then builds and ships it
- Database schema design and backend systems in TypeScript and Python, with API and workflow integrations; owns features across the stack
- Reusable tooling for teams: Tokalator (context and token budgeting) and agent skills for AI coding assistants

## Publications (3 papers + 1 patent pending)

### ACM CAIS '26 (Peer-Reviewed)
- Title: Multi-Agent Position Classification with Tool Orchestration: Use Case System for Occupational Taxonomy Mapping
- Authors: Vahid Faraji et al.
- Venue: ACM Conference on AI and Agentic Systems, San Jose, May 2026
- DOI: 10.1145/3786335.3813207
- URL: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3786335.3813207
- Page: https://vfaraji89.github.io/papers/cais-2026.html
- Key results: 95% accuracy on 14K+ positions, 72.5% faster classification, 41.8% fewer API calls
- Architecture: MCP-based multi-agent, planner, search, extraction, evaluation agents with shared caching

### arXiv: Tokalator

- ID: arXiv 2604.08290, April 2026
- URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08290
- Page: https://vfaraji89.github.io/papers/tokalator.html
- Contribution: Open-source toolkit for token-aware context management, Cobb-Douglas output-quality models, caching break-even analysis

### Multi-Agent Job Classification System
- Type: Research + production
- Stack: MCP, LangGraph, Subagent Architecture, AI Search, Caching
- Metrics: 95% accuracy, 14K+ positions, 72.5% faster, 41.8% fewer API calls
- Published: ACM CAIS '26

### Yapay Zekâ İzi: AI in 1.6M Job Ads (concept)
- Status: confidential Kariyer.net work, shown as a concept only; no data, link or product is public
- Completed: October 2026
- Scope: 1.6M job ads, 2022 (the GPT moment) to the first half of 2026
- Approach: an LLM pipeline reads every ad sentence by sentence, separates generative AI from classic AI and machine learning, normalises tool names to count which tools employers ask for, and reports by period, tool and sector with a validation page and the method. Quotes are kept verbatim from the ads.

### ProjectLens: Pricing Internal Tool (Kariyer.net)
- Type: Enterprise, internal
- Shipped: August 2026
- Team: Applied AI x Pricing & Revenue
- Stack: Applied AI, Microsoft Teams integration, Azure DevOps integration, SQL, workflow automation
- What it does: Takes a project request and manages the whole process end to end: effort calculation, pricing, proposal preparation, approval stage and follow-ups. Replaces a workflow where every pricing run meant a new Excel file.
- Notable: Read-only SQL console (only SELECT and WITH execute, each query runs in a rolled-back transaction on its own connection, nothing is writable) and a presentation mode that masks figures during screen shares.
- Metrics: 91% of manual effort eliminated; 64h manual baseline reduced to 5.5h; 59 hours freed (7.3 working days); 57h saved on pricing across 31 runs; 1.7h saved on request intake across 4 requests; 31 Excel files avoided.
- Measurement caveat: savings are modelled as 31 pricing runs x (2h - 10min) + 4 intake requests x (30min - 5min). The 2h manual baseline is a team estimate dated 2026-07-30, not an instrumented measurement.

## FAQ

Published here rather than on the page. Full text of each answer.

### Who is Vahid Faraji?

Vahid Faraji is a Senior Applied AI Specialist at Kariyer.net (ilab group) in Istanbul, Turkey. He has 8 years in industry (2 in applied AI, 6 in data products and business analysis) plus 4 years in research, and works at the boundary of research and production, publishing peer-reviewed work at ACM while deploying enterprise-scale multi-agent systems. His focus areas are multi-agent orchestration, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), and context engineering for large language models.

### What does Vahid Faraji actually build?

Production LLM agent systems for enterprises. Recent work includes an MCP-based multi-agent classification system that reached 95% accuracy on 14,000+ job positions while cutting classification time 72.5% and API calls 41.8%; an enterprise AI platform on LangGraph, MCP and Agno that reduced manual reporting workload 60% for 200+ internal users; and a 300M+ datapoint metadata architecture that became the retrieval and grounding foundation for later LLM deployments.

### Does Vahid Faraji build agent harnesses and evals?

Yes. He builds agent harnesses end to end: the execution loop, the tool interfaces the model calls, how context and memory are assembled, and the agent skills that package repeatable workflows. He makes quality measurable with evals built from real tasks, and uses traces and failure analysis to improve agent behaviour. In production he owns reliability, latency and cost, including resumable long-running tasks and tool-failure handling. He works spec-first, designs the database schema, and ships the feature across the stack in TypeScript or Python.

### What has Vahid Faraji published?

Three peer-reviewed and preprint papers. “Multi-Agent Position Classification with Tool Orchestration” is peer-reviewed and published in the ACM Digital Library (DOI 10.1145/3786335.3813207), presented at ACM CAIS '26 in San Jose. “Tokalator: A Context Engineering Toolkit for AI Coding Assistants” is on arXiv (2604.08290). “Leveraging LLMs For Turkish Skill Extraction” is on arXiv (2601.22885) and is the first systematic LLM benchmark for Turkish workforce analytics. One patent is pending.

### What is Tokalator?

Tokalator is an open-source context engineering toolkit built by Vahid Faraji, shipped as a VS Code extension and a web platform with 500+ installs under an MIT licence. It provides real-time token budgeting, tab relevance scoring, Cobb-Douglas output-quality modelling and caching break-even analysis across 17 LLMs. It is documented at tokalator.wiki and described in arXiv paper 2604.08290.

### Which technologies and frameworks does Vahid Faraji work with?

Agent and LLM stack: Anthropic Platform (Claude Agent SDK), Vercel AI SDK, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Model Context Protocol (MCP), LangGraph, Agno, and Langfuse and Arize for observability. Backend and data: Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, Text-to-SQL, DataHub, Azure Synapse, BigQuery and real-time pipelines. Frontend, deployment and tooling: Next.js deployed on Vercel, TypeScript 7 and VS Code extension development. Tracing and observability: Langfuse and Arize.

### Is Vahid Faraji available to hire or consult?

Yes. Open to Applied AI Engineer, Agentic AI Engineer, AI Platform Engineer, AI Solutions Architect and R&D Researcher roles, plus advisory engagements and enterprise AI training. His centre of gravity is building agent harnesses and evals and shipping them to production, backed by a peer-reviewed ACM publication and two arXiv papers. Based in Istanbul (GMT+3) and remote-friendly with distributed teams. Email vfaraji89@gmail.com or book a call; a condensed hiring summary is at https://vfaraji89.github.io/?hire

### Does Vahid Faraji do training and teaching?

Yes. He has trained 400+ people across 50+ courses, including an 18-hour Applied AI programme with Techcareer covering custom tool design, contextual system architecture, multi-agent coordination and production tool execution. He mentors on AI career paths for the TEV Foundation and gives guest lectures on enterprise prompt engineering at Kayseri University and Van University.

### What makes an applied AI profile like this different from an ML engineer?

The work is measured in shipped systems and business deltas rather than model metrics alone: accuracy on real taxonomies, latency and API-cost reductions, adoption counts, and workload removed. It spans the full path: problem framing, solution architecture, agent orchestration, evaluation and observability, and the data and metadata layer that makes retrieval trustworthy in the first place.

### Where is Vahid Faraji based and what languages does he speak?

Istanbul, Turkey (GMT+3). He speaks Turkish natively, English at C1 level, Spanish at instructor level, and basic Portuguese. He holds an M.A. in Economics from Ibn Haldun University with a thesis on real-time labour market analysis.
